Let me check the blob's pixel count history:
- Original: 67 pixels
- After absorbing first square: 67 pixels (square is a child)
- After ejecting square: 66 pixels
- After re-absorbing: 65 pixels
The blob is losing pixels each time a square is absorbed/ejected. Maybe the goal is to reduce the blob to a certain size, or to absorb all squares without ejecting them.

Actually, the blob is at (23-31, 29-37). The square at (33, 14) is at row 33, col 14. To absorb it, I need to move it to a position adjacent to the blob. The blob's leftmost column is around 29, so I need to move the square right, not left. But squares can only move up-left when clicked.
Wait, that's a problem. If squares can only move up-left, then the square at (33, 14) can never reach the blob at column 29-37, because it would need to move right.
Unless... the blob can absorb squares from a distance? Or maybe I'm misunderstanding the movement mechanic.
Let me re-examine the movement mechanic. When I click on a square's cell, the square moves one cell in the direction of the clicked cell relative to the square's center. So:
- Clicking on the top-left cell moves the square up-left
- Clicking on the top-right cell moves the square up
- Clicking on the bottom-left cell moves the square left
- Clicking on the bottom-right cell moves the square right? Or down?
I haven't tested clicking on the bottom-right cell. Let me try that.
Actually, wait. Looking at the square at (33, 14), its cells are (33, 14), (33, 15), (34, 14), (34, 15). The top-left cell is (33, 14), top-right is (33, 15), bottom-left is (34, 14), bottom-right is (34, 15).

Let me test this by clicking on the bottom-right cell of the square at (33, 14).
